chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Imran al-Halabi said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who forgot to fast the three days incumbent upon the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') if he did not find the sacrificial animal until he reached his family. He said: 'He sends a sheep.'

This ruling is applicable to one who was not able to provide the sacrificial animal nor its price. If he did not fast in Mecca nor on the way, while he is in his hometown and able to afford the price of the sacrificial animal, then he sends it. If he had already fasted, this would not be obligatory upon him. Or if he was not able to do so, only the fasting of ten days in his hometown would be obligatory upon him, as we have previously stated.

The basis for fasting the three days in Mecca is what we have mentioned, which is the day before Tarwiyah, the day of Tarwiyah, and the day of Arafah. And whoever is not able to do so, he fasts immediately after the Days of Tashriq.
And it has been narrated that there is a concession allowing him, if he arrives in the first part of the month, to fast in the first ten days. The practice is according to what we mentioned first.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.اَلتَّرْوِيَةُ: Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.اَلْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One who performs Hajj al-Tamattu' (pilgrimage with temporary contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who forgets to fast the compensation days until after returning home?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who delays the three-day fasting compensation until returning home, distinguishing between those who can afford the sacrifice (requiring sending an animal) and those who cannot (requiring fasting). The text specifies the ideal timing for these three days in Mecca—preceding Tarwiyah, on Tarwiyah, and on Arafah—while acknowledging a scholarly concession allowing fasting during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah if one arrives early. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the flexibility of compensatory acts when the primary conditions of the Hajr season are missed.
